q: The road foundation for modern highways construction, was developed by which of the following scientists?
e: While Macadam is scientifically considered the Father of Modern Roads for his method of using graded stones and drainage (which is the basis of modern flexible pavements), Telford specifically emphasized the  Foundation layer (large hand-packed stones). In the context of competitive exams (Loksewa), the answer is often accepted as Both.

q: The distance travelled by a moving vehicle during perception and brake reaction times, is known as:
e: Lag distance is the distance covered during the reaction time (t) of the driver. Stopping Distance = Lag Distance + Braking Distance.

q: Prime coat is done before laying tack coat in bituminous roads to:
e: A Prime Coat is a low-viscosity bitumen applied to an absorbent surface (like WBM) to plug capillary voids (seal pores) and bond loose particles.

q: The plinth area of building does NOT include:
o: Area of the walls at the floor level
Internal shaft for sanitary installation up to 2 sqm. in area
e: According to standard codes (IS 3861), cantilevered porches (which are not supported by columns/walls) are excluded from Plinth Area calculations.

q: The value of the property, without being dismantled, at the end of the useful life period is known as:
e: Salvation (Salvage) value is the value of the utility period without dismantling. Scrap value is the value of old material after dismantling.

q: The primary role of a contractor in a construction project is to:
o: Execute the work as per the contract agreement
e: The contractor is the party responsible for the physical execution and completion of the works in accordance with the specifications.

q: Muster Rolls are used for:
o: Paying wages of workers employed on daily basis
e: A Muster Roll is the fundamental record for attendance and payment of wages to daily labor (casual labor).

q: Bar charts are suitable for:
e: Bar charts are simple but lack the ability to show interdependencies effectively, making them suitable only for minor or simple works.

q: Which of the following is used for servicing and repairing of the aircraft?
e: A Hangar is a large enclosed structure used for housing, servicing, and repairing aircraft. An Apron is for parking/loading.

q: The runway orientation is made so that landing and take off are:
e: Aircraft generate lift more easily when moving against the wind (headwind), reducing the runway length required.

q: कोशी प्रदेशको चालु आवधिक योजनाको अन्त्यसम्ममा आर्थिक वृद्धिदर कति प्रतिशत पुर्‍याउने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ?
प्रदेश सञ्चित कोषको सञ्चालन कसले गर्दछ ?
अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले तल दिएका व्यक्ति मध्ये कुन व्यक्ति पदमा बहाल रहेको अवस्थामा त्यस्तो व्यक्ति उपर अनुसन्धान गर्न मिल्दैन ?
o: सैनिक ऐन बमोजिम कारबाही हुने व्यक्ति

q: प्रदेश लोक सेवा आयोगले लिने परीक्षाको पाठ्यक्रम समितिको संयोजक तलका मध्ये को रहने व्यवस्था छ ?
प्रत्यायोजन भएको अधिकारका सम्बन्धमा तलका कुन भनाई सही हो ?
o: काम फत्ते नभएसम्म फिर्ता गर्न मिल्दैन
जुनसुकै बखत फिर्ता गर्न सकिने छ
सरकार परिवर्तन हुनासाथ स्वतः खारेज हुन्छ

q: कोशी प्रदेश सरकारको प्रदेश अनुगमन तथा मूल्याङ्कन समितिको सदस्य सचिवको कार्य कसले गर्दछ ?
o: प्रमुख सचिव, मुख्यमन्त्री तथा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को कार्यालय
सचिव, आन्तरिक मामिला तथा कानुन मन्त्रालय
सचिव, आर्थिक मामिला तथा योजना मन्त्रालय

q: कोशी प्रदेश सुशासन (व्यवस्थापन तथा संचालन) नियमावली, २०७७ बमोजिम कोशी प्रदेशको एउटा सरकारी कार्यालयबाट अर्को सरकारी कार्यालयमा कार्य फर्छ्योट गर्न "अति जरुरी" लेखी प्राथमिकता तोकी आएको अवस्थामा कति दिनभित्र कार्य फर्छ्योट गरी पठाउनु पर्छ ?
स्थानीय तहमा काम गर्ने कर्मचारीले "ग" वर्गको भौगोलिक क्षेत्रमा कार्य गरेबापत प्रत्येक वर्ष कति अंक प्राप्त गर्दछन् ?
प्रदेश निजामती सेवाको रिक्त सातौँ तहको पदमा के कति प्रतिशत पदमा खुल्ला प्रतियोगिताद्वारा पदपूर्ति हुने कानुनी व्यवस्था रहेको छ ?
स्थानीय तहको गाँउसभा सदस्यको पदमा उम्मेदवार हुन पाउने उमेर कति हो ?
If the magnetic bearing of a line is 210° and magnetic declination at that place is 4° West, then true bearing of the line is,
e: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination (for West). 210° - 4° = 206°.

q: The method of determining the position of the plane table by sighting two known points is called:
e: Resection is the method of locating the station point occupied by the plane table by sighting known points.

q: Error in sighting and reading is termed as:
e: Errors arising from the limitations of human senses (sight, touch) are Personal Errors (e.g., reading a vernier incorrectly).

q: Contours are useful for:
o: The calculation of volumes of cut and fill
e: Contour maps provide elevation data allowing for the calculation of catchment areas, gradients (slopes), and reservoir capacities (volumes).

q: The strength of stone depends on:
e: The strength is influenced by mineral composition, density (packing), and geological structure.

q: The admixture added at the time of preparing the concrete mix to reduce the quantity of water and produce high strength concrete is known as:
e: Superplasticizers are high-range water reducers. They allow for a significant reduction in the water-cement ratio.

q: Efflorescence in bricks is caused by:
o: Soluble salts present in the brick
e: Efflorescence is the white powdery deposit on the surface caused by the crystallization of soluble salts (alkalis) when water evaporates.

q: The paint which gives illumination during night is called:
e: Fluorescent (or Phosphorescent) paints contain pigments that absorb light energy and emit it later, making them visible in the dark.

q: The bending moment diagram of a simply supported beam carrying uniformly distributed load over the entire span is a:
e: For a UDL, the Shear Force is linear, so the Bending Moment is parabolic (2nd degree).

q: A strut is a member which:
o: Is subjected to bending moment and shear force along with any axial force
Is subjected to axial compressive force predominantly
Is subjected to two shear force predominantly
e: A strut is a compression member in a truss or frame. Unlike a column, it can be horizontal, inclined, or vertical.

q: The ratio of weight of fluid to its volume at standard temperature and pressure is called:
e: Specific Weight (or Weight Density) = Weight / Volume.

q: The discharge over a rectangular weir is given by the formula:
e: The fundamental derivation integrates velocity (sqrt(2gh)) over the area, resulting in the term (2/3) C_d * L * sqrt(2g) * H^(3/2).

q: If velocities of fluid particles vary from point to point in magnitude and direction as well as from instant to instant, the flow is said to be:
e: This describes chaotic motion where parameters vary randomly with both space and time, which is the definition of Turbulent flow.

q: The relation between void ratio e, specific gravity G, water content w, and degree of saturation S is given by:
e: The standard soil mechanics relationship is Se = wG. Rearranging this gives e = wG/S.

q: The maximum dry density occurs at a particular water content, which is known as:
e: In compaction (Proctor test), the water content at which the soil achieves its densest state (Maximum Dry Density) is called OMC.

q: Which of the following is practically impermeable?
e: Clay has extremely small pores that are not interconnected, making it practically impermeable (Coefficient of permeability k < 10^-7 cm/sec).

q: The ultimate bearing capacity of soil is:
o: Total load on the bearing area
Safe load on the bearing area
e: Ultimate Bearing Capacity is the gross pressure at the base of the foundation at which the soil fails in shear.

q: An under reinforced section means:
o: Steel is provided at the under side only
Steel provided on one face only
e: In an under-reinforced section, the percentage of steel is low, ensuring the steel reaches its yield stress before the concrete crushes (ductile failure).

q: The amount of reinforcement for main bars in a slab is based upon:
e: Structural members are designed to resist the maximum effects of loads. Slabs are primarily flexural members, so main steel is calculated for Maximum Bending Moment.

q: Maximum percentage reinforcement in case of slabs is limited to:
e: According to IS 456, the maximum area of tension reinforcement should not exceed 4% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: Which type of foundation is most suitable for a building on black cotton soil?
e: Black cotton soil swells and shrinks drastically. Under-reamed piles are used to anchor the structure deep into stable soil zones.

q: In brick masonry, the bond produced by laying alternate headers and stretchers in each course is known as:
e: Flemish Bond consists of alternate Headers and Stretchers in the same course.

q: The method of damp proofing in which a layer of water repellent substance is provided between the source of dampness and part of structure adjacent to it, is known as:
e: Membrane damp proofing involves placing a physical barrier (membrane) like DPC (bitumen felt, plastic) to stop water rise.

q: Which method is the most common and cheaper for water curing?
e: For flat surfaces like slabs and pavements, constructing small clay bunds and filling them with water (Ponding) is the most efficient and cheapest method.

q: Break-pressure tank is generally provided in rural water supply schemes, if static head exceeds:
e: To prevent pipe bursting in hilly terrain, BPTs are installed to break the hydrostatic pressure to zero. The standard limit for HDPE pipes is often 60m.

q: The standard permissible limit of turbidity in drinking water is:
e: As per WHO and Nepal National Drinking Water Quality Standards (NDWQS), the acceptable limit is 5 NTU.

q: Before discharging the foul sewage into rivers, it is generally treated by:
e: Sewage treatment involves Physical (Screening, Sedimentation) and Biological (Oxidation) processes to reduce organic load before disposal.

q: The "outlet discharge factor" is the duty at the head of:
e: The Outlet is the point where water leaves the government channel and enters the farmer's channel (Water Course).

q: A structure constructed traverse to the river flow and extended from the bank in the river is called:
e: Spurs (or Groynes) are structures built perpendicular to the bank to deflect the current away from the bank, protecting it from erosion.

q: A structure constructed on an irrigation canal for the purpose of wasting some of its water is known as:
e: A Canal Escape is essentially a safety valve/side channel used to dispose of surplus water from the canal to prevent overtopping.
